blocks.text: The house is not large ,   , I am not Egyptian , , there is the elevator , to deny a nominal phrase the Arabic uses ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ , a word that combines like a verb and that puts the predicate to the accusative: . ⁧البَيْتُ لَيْسَ كَبِيرًا⁩ In this unit you learn it along with the vocabulary of the house and neighborhood, read real estate ads and describe the place where you live. blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-16), vocal synthesis script, a plant of your home, session with the tutor in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. deny a nominal sentence with ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ and place the predicate on the accusative;
2. conjugate ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ with all singular and plural pronouns;
3. choose between ⁧لَا⁩ (verb) and ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ (rated sentence);
4. use ⁧غَيْر⁩ to deny an adjective ( ⁧غَيْرُ مَفْرُوشَةٍ⁩ );
5. read a rental announcement and ask an agency for information;
6. describe your home and neighborhood in 70 words.

Three rules.
1. The predicate goes to the accusative: ⁧كَبِيرٌ⁩ → ⁧كَبِيرًا⁩ , ⁧مَفْرُوشَةٌ⁩ → ⁧مَفْرُوشَةً⁩ . It is the only change in form of sentence.
2. If the predicate is a complement with preposition or adverb ( ⁧فِي البَيْتِ⁩ , ⁧هُنَا⁩ ) nothing changes: the Preposition already holds his case.
3. ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ agrees with the subject: ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ for a male subject, ⁧لَيْسَتْ⁩ for a female, ⁧لَسْتُ⁩ for .

The subject pronoun generally fails, because ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ it contains: ⁧لَسْتُ مِصْرِيًّا⁩ I'm not Egyptian. Because the accused. ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ is originally a verb (to not be) of the same family as ⁧كَانَ⁩ • to be: (A2): These verbs leave the subject to the name and put the predicate to the accusative. You'll find it in A1-19. In texts without vowels the predicate to the accusative can only be seen when there is the aliif of tanwīn: . ⁧البيت ليس كبيرا⁩ It's a good clue to recognize a nominal negation.

⁧لَيْسَ⁩ it combines with the desinences of the perfect (which you will study in A1-18). When desinence begins by consonant, the root shortens in ⁧لَسْ⁩ -.
